Phase 64 impl @ 26003bc (branch phase/version-from-the-source-tree, still stacked on Phase 63's branch / PR #47; this phase is the last two commits: plan + this one). gate: see entry @ 26003bc — I did not run the full suite.

What changed
- tagteam/__init__.py: _source_tree_version(package_dir=None) and _resolve_version(); __version__ = tree version or metadata or '0.0.0+unknown'. tagteam/cli.py: _VERSION = {--version, -v, version} in read_only_refusal(), _dispatch() and HELP_TEXT.
- tests/test_version.py (new, 28 tests); tests/test_upgrade_smoke.py: test_installed_wheel_version_comes_from_metadata_not_a_source_tree.
- Docs: README command list, CLAUDE.md release flow, issues log (issue 2 and the --version bullet marked fixed), phase doc notes.

Your plan-approval guidance, as built
- Read-only routing: the aliases are in read_only_refusal() next to _HELP, matched after lower-casing (-V arrives as -v; 'VERSION' works too). test_version_command_is_a_read_under_read_only runs cli.main() with TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1 from an empty tmp dir outside any project: exit 0, nothing created, and asserts the guard still refuses 'setup'.
- Narrow reader: exactly one [project] table (header may carry a comment; the table ends at the next line starting with '['), exactly one name and one version assignment, each a plain double-quoted string, name == tagteam, version non-empty. Parametrized fall-back cases: foreign name, no version, commented-out version, duplicate version, duplicate name, single-quoted, empty, dynamic, no [project] table, two [project] tables, tool-table-only, blank file, invalid UTF-8; plus a directory at the path, a missing tree and a NUL in the path. Path resolution and read_text are inside one try/except Exception. A [tool.x] version placed before [project] is not picked up (own test).
- Wheel test: asserts _source_tree_version() is None in the wheel venv, and __version__ == importlib metadata == the version in the wheel FILENAME == pyproject's declared version; also 'python -m tagteam --version' from the wheel.
- The name check is documented as a layout guard, not a proof (phase doc).

Criterion 5 (read-only, from /tmp): tagteam --version -> 'tagteam 3.14.1' + the repo's package dir; tagteam state -> 'package 3.14.1'; pyproject 3.14.1. Honest caveat: the uv tool's metadata also says 3.14.1 today (re-installed after the bump), so the live check shows agreement, not the repair — the repair is proved by test_this_checkout_reports_what_pyproject_declares_whatever_the_metadata_says with metadata forced to 0.0.1.

Verified by me: focused only — test_version.py 28; test_version + test_upgrade_smoke 41; test_readonly + test_plugin + test_version 304; all passed.

GATE: PASS | scope 7 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2103 passed, 5 skipped, 7m40s)
checked: HEAD 26003bc

The CLI/read-only routing, wheel fallback check, and scope are sound. Two reproducible gaps remain in the narrow source parser:

1. tagteam/__init__.py:21: the optional header comment uses #.* under re.S, so it consumes the subsequent lines. A valid file containing:
[project] # package metadata
name = "tagteam"
version = "7.8.9"
returns None from _source_tree_version(), not 7.8.9. This contradicts the submission's explicitly supported commented header and restores the stale-metadata behavior after a harmless header comment. Bound the header comment to its own line (and keep table-body matching separate). Add a test with metadata forced stale, a commented project header, and a subsequent tool table; the source version must win.

2. tagteam/__init__.py:25-26: assignment counting only sees keys at column zero. This malformed/ambiguous project table is accepted as 7.8.9:
[project]
name = "tagteam"
version = "7.8.9"
 version = "9.9.9"
The approved conservative-reader policy requires duplicate/unsupported assignments to fall back, but the leading whitespace hides the duplicate from any_assignment. Detect horizontally indented name/version assignments when checking ambiguity, even if you choose not to support them as values. Add both indented duplicate-version and duplicate-name cases and assert metadata fallback. No general TOML parser is requested.

Verification: accepted GATE_PASS at 26003bc (2103 passed, 5 skipped); reviewer tests/test_version.py: 28 passed. Both cases above were reproduced using temporary pyproject files and the submitted _source_tree_version helper. git diff --check clean. Full suite not rerun; no implementation files changed.

Impl round 2 @ cbb3537 — both findings reproduced and fixed. gate: see entry @ cbb3537; I did not run the full suite.

1. Header comment. Under re.S my '(?:#.*)?' ran to end of file, leaving an empty table, so '[project] # package metadata' silently restored stale metadata. Now '(?:#[^\n]*)?' (the value-line comment got the same bound). New test_commented_project_header_still_wins_over_stale_metadata: metadata forced to 0.0.1, four header shapes (comment, tab+comment, trailing spaces, a comment containing brackets), followed by a [tool.x] table carrying its own version and name — the source version 7.8.9 wins in each.

2. Hidden duplicates. The ambiguity count was anchored at column zero. It is now '^[ \t]*["\']?key["\']?[ \t]*=' — indented and quoted spellings count as assignments — while the VALUE is still read only from the bare key at column zero (the shape release.py writes). Added fall-back cases: space-indented duplicate version (your example), tab-indented duplicate version, indented duplicate name, a quoted-key duplicate, and an indented-only version (not the release shape -> not sure -> metadata).

Checked that the new tests bite: with tagteam/__init__.py stashed back to round 1, 7 of them fail (the 4 duplicate cases and 3 commented headers); with the fix, tests/test_version.py is 37 passed. Only tagteam/__init__.py and tests/test_version.py changed since round 1. Live: tagteam --version from /tmp still prints 3.14.1.

Impl round 3 @ 57088cf — answers the round-2 GATE_BOUNCE. Code is unchanged from round 2 (tagteam/__init__.py + tests/test_version.py, commit 8 lines above); this commit adds only a docs entry. gate: see entry @ 57088cf; I did not run the full suite.

The bounce: 1 failed / 2111 passed / 5 skipped — tests/test_watcher_lock.py::test_start_watcher_reports_refusal_as_already_running, line 376, 'assert _wait(lambda: not _lock_free(project))': an externally spawned 'tagteam watch --mode notify' had not taken the project lock within 20 s. I classify it as a timing flake, and say plainly what that rests on and what it does not: (a) the round's diff cannot reach it other than through 'import tagteam' in the child, and the identical import path passed this test in the round-1 gate; (b) not reproduced — 6/6 passes alone at 0.5 s each, then the whole file 16/16; (c) it passed in the four earlier full-suite gate runs today; (d) load average was ~5.5 at the time. What I do NOT have is the cause: the child's output is not captured, so I cannot tell slow from refused from crashed. Logged as issue 10 in docs/tagteam-issues-release-and-venv-upgrade-2026-09-20.md with a suggestion to capture the child's output on failure. If this round's gate fails on the same test again I will treat it as real and investigate rather than resubmit.

Round-2 content, for your review (unchanged):
1. Header comment bounded to its own line ('(?:#[^\n]*)?'); test_commented_project_header_still_wins_over_stale_metadata — metadata forced stale, four header shapes, a following [tool.x] table with its own name/version; source version wins.
2. Ambiguity counted as '^[ \t]*["\']?key["\']?[ \t]*=' while the value is still read only from the bare key at column zero; new fall-back cases: space- and tab-indented duplicate version, indented duplicate name, quoted-key duplicate, indented-only version.
With __init__.py stashed back to round 1, 7 of the new tests fail; with the fix tests/test_version.py is 37 passed.

GATE: PASS | scope 7 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2112 passed, 5 skipped, 7m38s)
checked: HEAD 57088cf

Approved at 57088cf. Both round-1 findings are resolved: project-header comments are bounded to their own line, and indented/quoted duplicate assignments now cause metadata fallback. The added regressions cover commented headers followed by a tool table with conflicting metadata and the duplicate-key cases. Focused verification: tests/test_version.py, 37 passed; git diff --check 61765be clean.

Accepted the recorded Gatekeeper result at the same HEAD: 2112 passed, 5 skipped. Did not rerun the full suite. The round-2 watcher-lock failure did not recur in this gate; its cause remains unestablished and is explicitly recorded in issue 10 with a diagnostic follow-up. That uncertainty does not block this version-resolution change. No outstanding review findings.
